mission_04: Excellent! You have successfully implemented mixup augmentation. You learned how mixup creates interpolated training samples by combining pairs of examples with a Beta-distributed mixing coefficient. The resulting soft labels (continuous values between 0 and 1) provide a regularizing effect that improves model generalization. Mixup has been shown to reduce test error, improve calibration, and increase robustness to adversarial examples. The alpha parameter controls the strength of mixing: smaller alpha (e.g., 0.2) creates samples closer to the originals, while larger alpha creates more interpolated samples.
